## Natural history notes

A small bluet damselfly characterized by its slender body, clear wings held together over the back, and blue-and-black patterning, with males closely resembling other bluets and often requiring close inspection for confident identification. In Florida, it is found around freshwater ponds, lakes, streams, marshes, and other still or slow-moving wetlands, though it is less associated with clear sandy-bottom lakes than some similar species. Adults perch low on grasses, stems, and shoreline vegetation while hunting tiny flying insects, and the aquatic nymphs live among submerged plants or debris where they feed on small aquatic invertebrates.
